##  Undergraduate Studies 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/students)
Registration Fees | USD 200 per semester (Fall, Spring and Summer Session), paid in cash dollars and non-refundable.  
---|---  
Operational Fees | USD 300 per semester (Fall and Spring Semesters), paid in cash dollars and included in the first payment, as per the deadlines specified on the [Academic Calendar](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/calendar).   
  
NSSF membership fees | USD 94 per academic year, paid in fresh dollars at the market rate.  
Students already affiliated to the NSSF or to an equivalent fund (Cooperatives, military, judges and lawyers, Lebanese University, municipalities) are required to submit an official paper at the NSSF Delegate Office.  
Students who are not affiliated to the NSSF are required to fill in an exemption form at the NSSF Delegate Office.  
In both cases, this process should be completed before the scheduled deadline (See [Academic Calendar](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/calendar)).  
Students who fail to abide by this deadline will not be able to benefit from the NSSF coverage, and the above fees will be automatically credited to their account upon the 2nd payment of tuition fees.  
N.B.: Any person above 30 is exempted from the above fees and hence is not required to pass by the NSSF Delegate Office.  
Payment procedure | Students must settle their tuition fees in four installments per semester (Fall and Spring) and two installments (Summer Session).  
The total tuition fees***** can be calculated according to the table below. The first payment is equal to USD 1000 (including USD 200 registration fees) and must be settled as stated in the Academic Calendar.  
*** For the Fall Semester 2025-2026, tuition fees will be capped at 85% of the standard rate (payable in USD) and will return to their full value (100%) during the Spring Semester 2025-2026.**  
Failure to comply with the installment payment schedule as outlined in the Academic Calendar leads to a financial penalty calculated according to the amount due. The University will then determine a new payment date. Each student must ensure that their tuition fees are paid by the deadlines set by the University administration.  
  
Refunds | No refunds are granted unless in case of deregistration, and this as defined by the academic regulations.  
Financial aid  
| Throughout the Financial Aid Office, USEK provides help to students facing financial difficulties. And it continues to do so, according to its mission, through discounts. The relevant application should then be duly completed and submitted within the set deadlines. As such, students with financial problems can fill the [financial aid application](https://www.usek.edu.lb/student-service-offices/financial-aid-office) before the scheduled deadline (See [Academic Calendar](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/calendar)).

Note:
The cost of a credit is not related to the School/Faculty to which the student is affiliated, but rather to the School/Faculty that offers the related course.  
E.g.: A student registered in the Undergraduate Studies program at the Business School pays 350 USD for a business course credit, while he/she pays 137 USD for a language course credit.
  
  
These prices are applicable in all the USEK branches.  
  
The cost of a credit is subject to change; the administration reserves the right to review and modify fees every semester (Student Guide, D.2). ##  International Summer School 2025 
Discover Lebanon with USEK  
  
The USEK International Summer School, offers an enriching academic and cultural experience in the heart of Lebanon.  
Designed for international students, this two-week program aims to build bridges between cultures.  
  
Courses Offered:  
1. Arabic Crash Course  
2. Entrepreneurship and Startups in Lebanon  
3. Lebanese Heritage and Culture: A Journey Through Art, History, and Identity  
  

### Benefits
  * Academic Enrichment: Engage with dynamic courses that offer both theoretical insights and practical knowledge.
  * Cultural Immersion: Experience Lebanon through its rich traditions and vibrant social activities.
  * Global Networking: Connect with students and professionals from around the world.
  * Personal Growth: Develop skills that contribute to your academic and career aspirations.

  
  

### Program Details
Duration: **July 7 to 18, 2025**  
Cost: $1,500 (excluding travel, visa, accommodation, and insurance)  
Certificate: All participants receive a Certificate in Lebanese Heritage & Culture.  
  
[Click Here to Apply](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/login?redirect-to=/usek-international-summer-school-form/new)  
Registration is open until June 15, 2025. Limited spots available.  
  
For more information, kindly contact iao@usek.edu.lb or uclc@usek.edu.lb.  
  
Experience a summer like no other at USEK!  
Join us for an unforgettable journey at the USEK International Summer School 2025, and get culturally tanned.

## 
October 25, 2025
Beirut International Conference on Intercultural and Interfaith Dialogue for Sustainability – BICIDS 2025 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
Under the High Patronage of His Excellency, the President of the Republic of Lebanon, General Joseph Aoun, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) and the One Voice Foundation, in collaboration with the Faith for Earth Coalition (UNEP), are organizing the Beirut International Conference on Intercultural and Interfaith Dialogue for Sustainability.   
  
The event will take place on Saturday, October 25, 2025, from 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., at the John Paul II Amphitheater.   
  
Building on Lebanon’s unique history of coexistence, this conference reaffirms the country’s role as a global hub for dialogue and action on peace, pluralism, and sustainability. It offers a unique platform to bring together international leaders, academics, diplomats, and civil society to turn dialogue into concrete solutions for people and the planet.   
  
For registration, please click [here](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapply.usek.edu.lb%2Fusek-bicids-confirmation%2Fnew&data=05%7C02%7Ccynthiazeinoun%40usek.edu.lb%7Cd1369e34f72f4d98863308de08ab6c85%7C06d0a2c459b94cf8a36a9190f22cd1f6%7C0%7C0%7C638957729891914485%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=2doUUy%2BtSGf1e6hI0g9Ipz37VLdzh5VK5OEK2%2BRkBa8%3D&reserved=0).

## 
2025
Dr. Badih Baz’s First U.S. Patent Publication 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Technology Transfer Office (TTO) proudly announces the official publication of its first U.S. patent application by the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), marking a major achievement in USEK’s journey to foster impactful innovation.  
  
Key Highlights: 
  * Inventor: Dr. Badih Baz
  * Patent Title: Location Tracking Method and System
  * Publication Date: August 21, 2025
  * Functionality: A robust, centralized system for precise location tracking and attendance management, tailored for organizations of all sizes

  
  

### About the Technology Transfer Office: 
Dedicated to supporting researchers, translating creativity into tangible innovations, and driving technological advancement, the TTO showcases the dedication and ingenuity of USEK researchers and reinforces the University’s commitment to impactful innovation.

###  USEK School of Law and Political Sciences was inaugurated on November 10th, 1988, symbolically on the 40th anniversary of the Universal Declaration of the Human Rights.
From its beginnings, the School of Law and Political Sciences has always offered its students an exceptional education that consolidates the strength of tradition with the dynamism of the modern world.

## 
October 1, 2025
Law in the Movies: Absence of Malice 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
As part of its “Law in the Movies” series, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) invites you to the screening of Absence of Malice (1981), starring Paul Newman and Sally Field.   
  
The film follows a reporter who publishes a story based on a prosecutor’s false leak about a shop owner suspected of murder. It explores the tension between the public’s right to know and the protection of personal privacy, while also raising important ethical and legal questions about journalism, confidentiality, and freedom of speech.  
  
Hosted by the School of Law and Political Sciences, the event will take place on Wednesday, October 1, 2025, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., in the Conference Hall.  
  
A discussion between students and instructors will follow the screening.

## 
October 15, 2025
Inauguration Day: Presidential Investiture of Fr. Prof. Joseph Moukarzel 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
There are moments in the life of a university that embody both legacy and promise, moments when the past and the future converge in a shared spirit of service. With each new presidency, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik renews its mission to lead with purpose, building bridges between heritage and innovation, between faith and knowledge, between Lebanon and the world.   
  
In this spirit, the University will hold its first-ever Inauguration Day marking the investiture of Fr. Prof. Joseph Moukarzel as the seventeenth President of USEK.   
  
The event will take place on Wednesday, October 15, 2025, at 7:00 p.m., in the John Paul II Amphitheater.

## 
October 2, 2025
Lecture: Middle Eastern Diaspora in South America 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized an informative lecture titled “Middle Eastern Diaspora in South America”, delivered by Dr. Arlene Clemesha, Professor of Contemporary Arab History at the University of São Paulo, Brazil.  
  
Hosted by the School of Law and Political Sciences, the event took place on Thursday, October 2, 2025, from 11:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., at the Etienne Sacre Auditorium.  
  
The lecture provided an academic exploration of the historical and cultural dynamics that shaped the Middle Eastern presence in South America, offering valuable perspectives on migration, identity, and transnational connections.

## 
October 22, 2025
Lecture: The European Union and its Role in Lebanon 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) is organizing a lecture on “the European Union and its Role in Lebanon”, featuring Ms. Alessandra Viezzer, Head of Cooperation at the EU Delegation in Lebanon.   
  
Hosted by the School of Law and Political Sciences (SLPS), this event will take place on Wednesday, October 22, 2025, at 10:30 a.m., in the Fr. Étienne Sacre Auditorium.   
  
In keeping with a series of similar lectures delivered by guest speakers from the EU Delegation in Lebanon, Ms. Viezzer will be exploring with our students EU diplomacy and mediation with neighboring countries, such as Lebanon, and avenues for collaboration under the SLPS’s course “EU: Origins and Evolution”, in addition to internship opportunities within the various departments of the delegation.

## 
2025
New Invention Filed at USEK: LSA Tool 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Technology Transfer Office is proud to announce the filing of a new invention: the Landscape Sustainability Assessment (LSA) Tool. This first-of-its-kind quantitative educational and diagnostic tool is designed to evaluate and promote landscape sustainability through four dimensions: ecological, social, economic, and perceptual. By transforming theoretical models into practical, data-driven insights, the LSA Tool empowers institutions, policymakers, and stakeholders to make informed decisions that enhance and preserve vital landscape resources.  
  
**Key Highlights**
  * Inventors: Prof. Nabil M. Nemer and Dr. Roula Y. Aad
  * Invention Name: LSA – Landscape Sustainability Assessment Tool
  * Functionality: An AI-powered decision-support system that collects and analyzes environmental data to assess the sustainability of landscapes.

  
**Key Features**
  * AI-powered analysis
  * Advanced environmental data collection
  * Multidimensional sustainability indicators
  * Real-time monitoring
  * Applicable to diverse ecosystems (reserves, farms, forests, cities)
  * Decision-support dashboard for policymakers and researchers

  
  
**About the Technology Transfer Office**  
Dedicated to supporting researchers, translating creativity into tangible innovations, and driving technological advancement, the TTO showcases the dedication and ingenuity of USEK researchers and reinforces the University’s commitment to impactful innovation.

## 
October 20 – November 21
Preparatory Session for the Controllers and Auditors 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The School of Law and Political Sciences at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) is organizing a Preparatory Session for the Controllers and Auditors Entrance Exam at the Court of Accounts.   
  
Led by experts in the field, this comprehensive session is tailored for recent graduates and students in law, business, or related fields. Participants will gain practical insights, targeted strategies, and essential knowledge to prepare effectively for the entrance exam.   
  
**Why enroll in this preparatory session?**
  * Understand the exam’s structure, its format, and key components 
  * Gain knowledge in public accounting and control 
  * Benefit from expert guidance and strategic preparation for exam success 

  
  
**Session Details**   
Date: October 20 – November 21   
Location: Court Room (Building B – GF)   
  
**Fees**
  * USEK active students: 200$ 
  * USEK alumni: 250$ 
  * External participants: 300$ 

  
**  
Registration and Payment**  
1. Go to the APPLY platform (apply.usek.edu.lb).   
2. Navigate to the Academic Applications section (apply.usek.edu.lb/academic-applications).   
3. Under the Law and Political Sciences section, locate the Controllers and Auditors Preparatory Session registration card and click on Apply Now.   
4. Log in using one of the following:   
- MS Office 365 account   
- Gmail account   
- USEK account (ID and Password)

## 
September 23 & 24, 2025
Workshop: Recovery and Healing – A Response to Sexual Violence 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) was proud to host the fourth workshop of the “Women, Peace, and Security” (WPS) project, titled “Recovery and Healing – A Response to Sexual Violence”, led by Stacy Schultz from George Mason University, Virginia.  
  
Organized by the School of Law and Political Sciences, this event took place on Tuesday, September 23, 2025, at the Kaslik Campus (HS315) and on Wednesday, September 24 at Zahle RUC, from 9:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.  
  
About the WPS   
The WPS agenda is a global framework recognizing the vital role of women in preventing conflict, promoting peace, and contributing to post-conflict recovery. Established over twenty years ago by a United Nations Security Council resolution, WPS focuses on four key priorities: protecting women from violence, ensuring access to relief and recovery, fostering participation in peacebuilding, and advancing security efforts. The United States has been a leading advocate, enacting the first national WPS law and framing its implementation as both a moral obligation and a strategic priority. Lebanon, despite adopting a national plan for WPS, continues to face obstacles due to political instability, economic collapse, and persistent conflicts.  
  
The program sought to address such challenges by empowering Lebanese youth, particularly women, as future leaders. The initiative comprised three components: 
  * workshops led by experts to introduce WPS concepts;
  * interviews with young women across Lebanon to capture their perspectives and challenges;
  * a documentary film weaving these insights into an educational and awareness-raising tool.

  
  
Together, these efforts amplified women’s voices, promoted their role in society, and strengthened Lebanon’s path toward peace and democratic development.  
  
This program was funded by the U.S. Embassy in Beirut.

##  Regional University Centers 
Committed to providing higher educational opportunities for students who would otherwise not have access to it, USEK’s three regional university centers (RUCs) in Lebanon act as instructional locations who offer courses for students who want to earn a degree within their communities and achieve their educational and career goals.  
  
Students can benefit from studying in a small learning environment, developing meaningful relationships with faculty, attentive to their needs, in a convenient location.  
  
For information about the courses per program offered at the RUCs please go to [Find a Program](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/academics#programs) and select the relevant Campus.  
  
USEK Regional Campus Benefits: 
  * Small classes with experienced faculty members who are practicing professionals in their field
  * Convenient schedules leaving you enough time to fit in work or family responsibilities
  * Access to full-time staff to assist students with financial aid, registration or general academic program questions
  * High-tech resources
  * Convenient parking

  
As of Fall 2024, operations have been suspended in Regional University Centers Chekka and Rmeich temporarily. The university teach out policy has been applied accordingly.   
  

[ZAHLE RUC](javascript:;)
Zahle enrolled its first students in September in 2000/2001. Located 55km east of Beirut the campus Zahle lies at the meeting point between the Lebanon mountains and the striking Beqaa plateau, and is famous throughout Lebanon and the region for its pleasant climate, numerous riverside restaurants and quality arak.  
  
**Why Zahle?**  
The largest of the regional centers, Zahle offers courses in academic programs across most core disciplines, including applied arts, architecture, agriculture, business and commercial sciences, engineering, fine arts, food sciences, humanities, law, philosophy, and sciences.  
  
RUC Zahle offers undergraduate courses in different disciplines such as: 
  * Architecture and Design
  * Business
  * Computer Science
  * Civil / Mechanical Engineering
  * Engineering Sciences – Food Engineering
  * Education 
  * Law
  * Biochemistry
  * Nutrition and Dietetics

  

### Degrees
**School of Law & Political Sciences**  
Law Degree (137 credits) (Open for Admission)  
  
**USEK Business School**  
Bachelor of Business Administration (99 credits)  
Emphasis:  
- Audit (Open for Admission with a minimum no. of entering class)  
- Finance (Open for Admission with a minimum no. of entering class)  
- Management and Entrepreneurship (Open for Admission with a minimum no. of entering class)  
  
**School of Architecture and Design**  
Bachelor & Master of Architecture (102 out of 190 credits) (Open for Admission)  
Bachelor of Arts in Design and Applied Arts (108 credits) (Open for Admission)  
Bachelor of Arts in Communication and Visual Arts (108 credits) (Open for Admission)  
  
**Faculty of Arts and Sciences**  
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (96 credits) (Open for Admission)  
Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry (96 credits) (Open for Admission)  
Bachelor of Arts in Education (96 credits) | Emphasis: Basic Education (Open for Admission)  
Bachelor of Science in Human Nutrition and Dietetics (96 credits) (Open for Admission)  
  
**School of Engineering**  
Bachelor of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering (68 out of 146 credits) (Open for Admission)  
Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering (68 out of 146 credits) (Open for Admission)  
Bachelor of Science in Engineering Sciences – Food Engineering (107 credits) (Open for Admission with a minimum no. of entering class)

[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/admissions?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/alumni?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/career-center?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/financial-aid?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/registrar?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/information-technology?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/counseling-and-accessibility-office?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/student-affairs-office?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/international-affairs?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/library?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/eits?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/sports-department?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/students/frequently-asked-questions/national-social-security-fund?parent=1)
[1- Where can I find the credit prices and the payment procedure?](javascript:;)
Credit fees vary according to your program(s) of interest. You can check all the [fees](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/university-fees/undergraduate-studies-1) on the USEK website. As for the payment procedure, up until now, 70% of the tuition fees must be settled in fresh USD, and the remaining fees will be waived. Please note that the payment procedure is subject to change.
[2- Are candidates with an SAT score eligible to apply for a scholarship?](javascript:;)
SAT scores may exempt you from sitting for the English Proficiency Test and the program-specific exams only. You can check the [required scores per program](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/admission/online-admission-requirements) on the USEK website.
[3- Do candidates who get high grades on the official exams benefit from a scholarship?](javascript:;)
Candidates must apply first during the Early Admission period (February-April) to be eligible for upgrading their scholarship based on the official exams results at a later stage. All dates and deadlines are available on the USEK website.
[4- Am I eligible to apply for an admission with scholarship during the Spring Semester?](javascript:;)
Unfortunately, scholarships are valid only if you apply directly for the Fall Semester after graduating from school.
[5- What is the admissions procedure to apply to USEK?](javascript:;)
You must submit your [online application](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/academic-applications) available on the USEK website: and attach the [required documents](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/admission/online-admission-requirements) so that we can check your eligibility accordingly.
[6- What are the required study materials for the entrance exam(s)?](javascript:;)
You can send an email to admissions@usek.edu.lb and we will be sending you the required chapters and samples accordingly.
[7- How does the Hybrid education system work?](javascript:;)
USEK follows the American credit system. Some programs are purely offered in English, while others can be hybrid (with some courses in French and others English depending on the program and the course offering for each semester).
[8- Can English-educated candidates apply for a hybrid program?](javascript:;)
Yes, you can, However, you may still need to validate French remedial courses and communication skills. Since some courses may be offered solely in French, proficiency in this language could be essential for a successful experience within hybrid programs.
[9- What are the requirements to register as a Freshman student?](javascript:;)
To apply for the Freshman program, you must submit a permit of study, your school diploma, and a minimum SAT score of 1000. You can submit your [online application](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/academic-applications) on the [USEK website](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/admission/online-admission-requirements) and attach the required documents and we will check your eligibility accordingly.
[10- Can I register as a Freshman student if I fail the official exams?](javascript:;)
Candidates who fail the official exams are not eligible to apply for the Freshman program. Once their exams passed, they can re-apply as sophomore. You can check your eligibility to apply as a freshman student via this [link](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/admission/freshman).
[11- What is the procedure to reactivate my file?](javascript:;)
If you activated your account but did not register for any courses, you must send an email to admissions@usek.edu.lb. However, if you register for any courses, you must to submit a Readmission request to the Office of the Registrar within the deadlines set on the [Academic Calendar](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/calendar).
[12- What if I am unable to attend the orientation session?](javascript:;)
The orientation session is mandatory and is very helpful to ensure a smooth registration process. However, if you cannot attend it, please refer to the Students Affairs Office at: sao@usek.edu.lb.
[13- Can I take my entrance exams online?](javascript:;)
Entrance exams are held only on campus, not online. You can reschedule your exam to another date, if available.
[14- How can I submit a transfer request if I have an LT degree?](javascript:;)
Only a TS degree can be taken into consideration if you have a grade average of 12 and above. You can submit your [online application](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/academic-applications) on the [USEK website](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/admission/online-admission-requirements) and attach the required documents so that we can check your eligibility accordingly.
[15- What are the consequences of breaching my contract with Notre Dame de Secours (NDS) University Hospital?](javascript:;)
As mentioned in the signed contract, you must repay all your tuition fees if you decide to breach the contract. For more info: accountsreceivable@usek.edu.lb.
[16- What is the admissions procedure for submitting a transfer request to USEK?](javascript:;)
To initiate the process, you must submit your [online application](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/academic-applications) on the [USEK website](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/admission/online-admission-requirements) and attach the required documents so that we can check your eligibility accordingly. Subsequently, we will conduct a thorough study of your file to determine the transferability of courses.   
  
Please note that a maximum of 49% of your credits can be considered for transfer.   
  
Details about transferred courses cannot be provided in advance as they are contingent on the file study decision.
[17- Can I apply for two majors at the same time?](javascript:;)
You can activate one program only through the Admissions Office. However, as an active USEK student, you can later submit a double major request at the Office of the Registrar at registrar@usek.edu.lb within the deadlines mentioned on the [Academic Calendar](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/calendar).
[18- Are USEK degrees recognized?](javascript:;)
Your USEK degree allows you to apply to master programs in other national universities. However, each university has its own admissions requirements; hence, it is preferable to refer to your university of interest.
[19- Can I defer my admission after I have been accepted?](javascript:;)
Your acceptance is valid for two consecutive semesters only. You can postpone it to the consecutive semester only without having to submit the online application again. However, if you do not register at all during the Fall and Spring semesters, you will have to submit a new application form to be studied again according to the admission conditions.
[20- Does USEK offer online certificates?](javascript:;)
You can refer to the [USEK Continuing Learning Center](https://www.usek.edu.lb/uclc) (UCLC) on the USEK website or send an email at: uclc@usek.edu.lb.

##  Scholarships and Financial Aid 
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) is committed to supporting our students, faculty, staff, and their families. Through our network of agreements, partnerships, donations, and scholarship programs, we help ensure that every student facing financial constraints receives the necessary assistance. Our aim is to empower all students to pursue their education unhindered by financial burdens.  
  
For more details on the terms and conditions for any type of reduction, please contact us at: supportcenter@usek.edu.lb.  
  
  

[Reductions and Agreements](javascript:;)
  * Students can apply for Financial Aid according to the terms and conditions described under the [FAO section](https://www.usek.edu.lb/student-service-offices/financial-aid-office)
  * Siblings who are simultaneously registered at USEK: refer to the [FAO section](https://www.usek.edu.lb/student-service-offices/financial-aid-office) - Submission of an Allowance Request for Siblings
  * Brother, sister, nephew, or niece of a Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM) member: refer to the [FAO section](https://www.usek.edu.lb/student-service-offices/financial-aid-office) - Submission of a Discount Request for OLM Relatives
  * Alumni of OLM schools (refer to the Admissions Office)
  * USEK employee ([online application](https://s.usek.edu.lb/wf/main.aspx?pid=DISC_TUITION)) (refer to the HR)
  * Son or daughter of a USEK employee ([online application](https://s.usek.edu.lb/wf/main.aspx?pid=DISC_TUITION)) (refer to the HR)
  * Full-time faculty at USEK / Son or daughter of a full-time faculty member at USEK ([online application](https://s.usek.edu.lb/wf/main.aspx?pid=DISC_TUITION)) (refer to the HR)
  * Full-time faculty at USEK / Son or daughter of a part-time faculty member at USEK ([online application](https://s.usek.edu.lb/wf/main.aspx?pid=DISC_TUITION)) (refer to the HR)
  * Part-time faculty at USEK / Son or daughter of a part-time faculty member at USEK (1h and more) ([online application](https://s.usek.edu.lb/wf/main.aspx?pid=DISC_TUITION)) (refer to the HR)
  * Son or daughter of a USEK employee / Son or daughter of a full-time faculty member at USEK / Son or daughter of a part-time faculty member at USEK who is registered in the School of Music ([online application](https://s.usek.edu.lb/wf/main.aspx?pid=DISC_TUITION)) (refer to the HR) 
  * INDEVCO employees and their children ([online application](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=xKLQBrlZ-EyjapGQ8izR9givrHmDHLxPkNsXFuOsLnBUOURMQ0RPN1Y4Q05WUDNKTUJBT1BRS1ZQNi4u))
  * MTV employees and their children ([online application](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=xKLQBrlZ-EyjapGQ8izR9givrHmDHLxPkNsXFuOsLnBUOURMQ0RPN1Y4Q05WUDNKTUJBT1BRS1ZQNi4u)). 
  * Students included in the USEK/LA, USEK/ISF, USEK/GS, USEK/LC, USEK/SS, USEK/Judges agreements ([online application](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=xKLQBrlZ-EyjapGQ8izR9givrHmDHLxPkNsXFuOsLnBUOURMQ0RPN1Y4Q05WUDNKTUJBT1BRS1ZQNi4u))
  * Children of CHUNDS full-time employee and nursing staff ([online application](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=xKLQBrlZ-EyjapGQ8izR9givrHmDHLxPkNsXFuOsLnBUOURMQ0RPN1Y4Q05WUDNKTUJBT1BRS1ZQNi4u))
  * Children of CCJ employees/teachers ([online application](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=xKLQBrlZ-EyjapGQ8izR9givrHmDHLxPkNsXFuOsLnBUOURMQ0RPN1Y4Q05WUDNKTUJBT1BRS1ZQNi4u))
  * Students part of the Student Job Program (refer to the Student Affairs Office)
  * Students who are part of the USEK Talents’ Program (refer to the Student Affairs Office)
  * Students who are members of a USEK sports team (refer to the Sports Department)


[Scholarships](javascript:;)
### Merit Scholarship
[USEK Merit Scholarships](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/student-service-offices/registrar-office-1/merit-scholarship-regulations?parent=1) are awarded to undergraduate and graduate students who demonstrate exceptional academic performance and conduct.  
  

### Excellence Scholarship
Applicants must sit for the English Proficiency Test and have a minimum English level equivalent to Level 2. Applicants who are assigned a Level 1 English remedial course must register in the Foundation Program first. Once completed, they can benefit from the scholarship offered, if any, during the first sophomore year. Therefore, the scholarship is not applicable for the Foundation Program.  
  
You can find below more details about the potential scholarship percentages.  
  
  
All applicants with a general average ≥14/20 in Grades 10 and 11 (with no ranking) and ≥15/20 (for Engineering or Architecture programs) are entitled to an excellence scholarship as follows:  
  
General Average ≥14 (with no ranking) | 20% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.  
  
---|---  
General Average ≥15 (with no ranking) | 30% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.  
  
General Average ≥16 (with no ranking) | 40% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.  
  
General Average ≥17 (with no ranking) | 60% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.  
  
  
  
All Candidates with a general average ≥15/20 for BT1 and BT2 (with no ranking) are entitled to an excellence scholarship as follows:  
  
General Average ≥15 (with no ranking) | 30% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.  
  
---|---  
General Average ≥16 (with no ranking) | 40% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
General Average ≥17 (with no ranking) | 60% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.  
  
  
  
Students enrolled in the British curriculum can apply for an admission with scholarship if they present their predicted G12 scores in addition to the statement of results for years 10 and 11 (IGCSE level) as per the following:  
  
2 grade A on IGCSE level over 5 subjects (excluding Languages and D grades) | 30% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
---|---  
3 grade A on IGCSE level over 5 subjects (excluding Languages and D grades) | 40% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
4 grade A on IGCSE level over 5 subjects (excluding Languages and D grades) | 60% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
  
  
Students enrolled in the International Baccalaureate can apply for an admission with scholarship if they present their predicted G12 scores as per the following:  
  
32-33 points  | 20% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
---|---  
34-35 points  | 30% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
36-37 points  | 40% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
38-39 points  | 60% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration and operational fees (500 USD) and NSSF fees.   
40+ points  | 100% covering tuition fees for one academic year (Fall and Spring semesters), excluding registration fees (200 USD) and NSSF fees.   
  
  
PS: Applicants must fulfill the program requirement (HL/SL) in addition to the points mentioned in the table above to benefit from the scholarship.   
  

### Upgraded Scholarship
Applicants who benefit from an excellence scholarship can get an upgrade in 3 cases:   
  
**a. Based on the official exams results:**  
- Applicants who pass the Lebanese Baccalaureate or an equivalent diploma with an average ≥17 for Lebanese Baccalaureate and ≥17 for the French Baccalaureate can benefit from a 75% scholarship upgrade, provided that they apply during the Early Admission period and fulfill admission requirements.   
  
**b. Based on Grade 12 ranking:**  
- Applicants who rank first by the end of Grade 12 can benefit from a 100% scholarship covering the whole program, provided that they meet the needed regulations and conditions. The scholarship does not cover registration and NSSF fees, or the Summer Session.  
  
**c. Based on SAT scores:**  
- An additional 10% will be applied to the excellence scholarship for holders of SAT scores ≥1350.  
- Only students who applied during the Early Admission period and received an excellence scholarship can benefit from an additional percentage based on their SAT scores.

##  Student voice 
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) places great importance on the academic participation of students in the decision-making process, as it believes that students should contribute to the enhancement of academic programs and to the improvement of students’ campus life and learning experience.   
  
Feedback on the academic experiences of students is communicated through a student council in each academic unit, which allows students to raise any concerns over academic issues such as course content, teaching methods, assessment criteria, resources, and feedback, and will also provide testimonials of good practice.  
  
Student council will report directly to the head of the concerned academic unit/associate dean and director of the Student Affairs Office, and consequently to the president.  
  

  * ### Call for Candidacy
By the end of each academic year, a call for candidacy will be sent by email to all students. (dates to be defined in the University’s Academic Calendar).
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/current-students/student-participation-policy/call-for-candidacy)
  * ### Eligibility
Students considered eligible are those who meet the following criteria: Undergraduate Students: Have already accomplished 30 credits of their program; Have a cumulative GPA of 75/100...
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/current-students/student-participation-policy/eligibility)
  * ### Selection Process
Prospective student council members are invited to fill out an online application within the relevant deadlines (mentioned in the Academic Calendar). Applicants will receive a confirmation...
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/current-students/student-participation-policy/selection-process)
  * ### Student Council 2023-2024

##  USEK Model United Nations Chapter (UMC) 
[ ![Welcome Message](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/59649Image1.gif?v=202502131106) Welcome Message ](javascript:;)
[ ![About the Chapter](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/59643Image1.png?v=202502131059) About the Chapter ](javascript:;)
[ ![Board Members](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/59647Image1.png?v=202502131101) Board Members ](javascript:;)
[ ![Our Programs](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/60311Image1.gif?v=202502131112) Our Programs ](javascript:;)
[ Contact Us ](javascript:;)
Welcome to the USEK Model United Nations Chapter (UMC)— where tomorrow’s leaders are made today.   
  
This is your platform for growth in public speaking and leadership. UMC’s mission? To empower you with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in the world of international relations and diplomacy.   
  
As the founder, I can assure you that success follows those who are dedicated, engaged, and embrace every opportunity to learn.  
  
Now, it’s your turn to rise—let’s shape the future together!  
  
Kevin Awkar  
Founder  
  

### Mission
UMC’s mission is to forge future leaders by developing our member’s knowledge and competencies for diplomatic simulations, and public speaking skills. Moreover, our main purpose is to promote socio-political education through international affairs and inter-governmental policies; hence, shaping students into leaders and thinkers.   
  

###  Vision
We aim to change the world with one delegate at a time! We believe that MUN is an opportunity for all students to find a new path that can showcase potential and progress. Thus, we envision growing within the USEK community and adding achievements to the portfolio of each member.   
  

### Founding of the Chapter
The Chapter was founded by Kevin Awkar in 2021, with the vision of forging future leaders. As a results-driven professional skilled in team leadership, program management, and public speaking, Kevin applies his expertise to drive impactful partnerships and deliver successful outcomes.  
  
Holding a Master’s degree in Middle Eastern Studies (with honors) and a BA in Political Science from USEK, he combines academic insight with professional experience to address complex global challenges.  
  
Recipient of the Diplomacy and Outstanding Delegation Awards at the WFUNA International Model United Nations 2019 in New York, Kevin is an accomplished expert in building high-performing teams and executing sustainable projects. After several years of growth and advancement, he successfully transitioned the Chapter to a new generation of leaders, who are now chairing the Chapter.  

**Christopher El Murr  
Chairperson**  
  
Christopher is an inspiring and effective leader with a strong commitment to teamwork. His experience in concept development and the implementation of developmental programs allows him to lead the Chapter’s projects with a strong focus on growth. With a background in Clinical Psychology, he tailors UMC’s programs to be accessible to a wide range of university students with one goal envisioned: Forging Future Leaders.  
  
Chris joined UMC in 2021 and quickly progressed to become the Head of Trainings, then Head of Programs, and now the Chairperson of UMC. He aims to lead the Board towards collective growth and development, ensuring that UMC continues to foster a healthy and inclusive environment.  
  
Chris is a proven problem-solver with strategic capacities and an unwavering readiness to find solutions to overcome obstacles. His key to success lies in his belief in the power of teamwork thanks to the rich and diverse team at UMC.  
**  
Joy Topalian  
Lead Executive**  
  
Joy, a passionate leader and innovator with a degree in Business Management and Entrepreneurship, exemplifies excellence in every endeavor. A recipient of the Amazon Award for Business, she combines a passion for entrepreneurship with a proven track record of accomplishments. In her role as Lead Executive at UMC, Joy plays a key role in driving innovation, change, and professional growth.  
  
Her journey with the USEK MUN Chapter began in 2021, where she quickly distinguished herself as a delegate, earning her first MUN Forum 1 Conference award while representing the EU Delegation. Over the years, her dedication and performance have earned her numerous recognitions, including the Position Paper Award.  
  
By 2023, Joy’s leadership and vision led to her appointment as Lead Executive, where she spearheaded transformative initiatives such as the Level-Up Leadership Program, the Jumpstart Program, and other high-impact events. Driven by a commitment to empowering students, Joy inspires others to unlock their full potential and achieve remarkable success.  
**  
Diana Al Hayek  
Head of Logistics and Communications**  
  
Diana is a third-year biochemistry student at USEK. Her academic journey has been guided by a profound passion for science and relentless pursuit of knowledge.  
  
Her commitment to personal growth and community involvement led her to embark on a journey of self-development at UMC, growing with the Chapter to become the Head of Communications and Logistics.  
  
Beyond UMC, Diana is engaged in several volunteer activities and serves as the student representative of USEK’s Zahle RUC. In all her endeavors, she strives to leave an impact on society, advocating for positive change.  
  
**Ziad Chalhoub  
Head of Programs**   
  
Ziad is a dedicated law student with a deep commitment to leadership, diplomacy, and driving meaningful change. Since joining the University’s MUN chapter in 2021, Ziad has actively contributed to its growth, culminating in his current role as Head of Programs. In this position, he leads the design and execution of professional, high-impact initiatives, ensuring members are equipped with the necessary skills to engage in constructive dialogue on global issues.  
  
Having participated in numerous MUN conferences and earning several leadership certificates, Ziad has cultivated expertise in public speaking, negotiation, and planning.   
  
His professional approach to problem-solving and teamwork reflects a strong focus on excellence and innovation, inspiring others to actively engage in diplomacy and global affairs. With aspirations to leave a positive mark on the world, Ziad brings not only skill and dedication but also a unique ability to make every experience both impactful and enjoyable.  
  
**Alexandre Razzouk  
Head of Programs  
**  
Alexandre Razzouk is a third-year bachelor’s student in International Relations at USEK. Passionate about diplomacy and leadership, he has gained extensive experience in Model United Nations programs, serving as a delegate, Training Coordinator, and Advisor for USEK delegations at programs such as BEYMUN.   
  
His contributions to public speaking, speechwriting, and research have earned him multiple awards in recognition of his skills and dedication. Alexandre is also actively involved in leadership programs and ecological initiatives, highlighting his commitment to building inclusive, resilient, and sustainable, global communities.  
  
Beyond academics, Alexandre is a member of the USEK Tennis Team, showcasing his discipline and team-oriented mindset. Balancing rigorous studies, extracurricular activities, and competitive sports, he exemplifies a well-rounded approach to personal and professional growth. His strong organizational and interpersonal skills position him as a promising future leader in the field of international relations.
**Level-up Leadership Program 2023 (LULP2023)**  
LULP 2022’s success paved the way for a return in 2023, reinforcing its role as a catalyst for leadership development. Extending beyond USEK, LULP2023 welcomed 90 students from different universities across Lebanon.  
Inspired by the rise of Artificial Intelligence, LULP 2023 focused on tackling the connection between AI and sustainable development.   
Participants took part in a series of practical training sessions designed to boost their skills and deepen their understanding of how AI can improve cities and communities. This approach, paired with a hands-on Model United Nations conference, allowed students not only to come up with ideas, but also to actively put them into action. LULP’s expansion in 2023 shows its commitment to spreading leadership development and knowledge-sharing to a wider audience beyond a single institution.  
  
**Jumpstart: Skill-Full Day**  
“Jumpstart: Skill-full Day” was a one-day developmental program in partnership with the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom (FNF) and supported by USEK.  
The program featured top-tier expert speakers who shared their insight on personal and professional growth in the fields of team management, pitching, and civic engagement.  
Participants worked in groups, under the theme of development in civic engagement, to create solutions to enhance student life at USEK.   
The 3 winning teams received support to make their ideas come to life.  
  
**Level-up Leadership Program 2022 (LULP2022)**  
The Level-up Leadership Program (LULP) was a USEK Model United Nations Chapter (UMC) initiative in collaboration with the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom (FNF)and with the support of USEK. This MUN-based program was designed to mold students into future leaders, equipping them with essential skills and insights.  
The program consisted of several accelerator training sessions followed by an MUN simulation targeting Global Goal 16 of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.   
Winners received several valuable awards, with the 3 laureates of our Leadership Award winning a trip to Germany.  
  
**How Future Leaders Find a Job**  
“How Future Leaders Find a Job” was a two-day interactive workshop at USEK’s Zahle RUC designed to empower over 40 participants with essential soft and hard skills, including job search strategies and insights into the dynamic world of professional life.  
**  
Simulation of Collaborative Gatherings (SCG)**  
Following the UMC Program, the most dedicated participants went on to become UMC members following a new phase of immersive development through multiple training sessions. These specialized sessions solidified their skills and fortified their understanding of effective leadership. The practical application of the participants’ enhanced abilities in an MUN final conference became a hallmark of the UMC experience, with outstanding delegates becoming part of the UMC team.  
  
**UMC Program (UMCP)**  
The UMC Program was a comprehensive training program where participants engaged in weekly sessions dedicated to developing public speaking, leadership, and conflict resolution skills. Throughout the program, participants delved into the art of effective communication, explored the principles of diplomacy, and mastered critical thinking strategies. Dedicated mentors and professional public speakers led this journey, which concluded with a final MUN simulation.

# School of Medicine and Medical Sciences
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/academics)
### In accordance with the mission of the Lebanese Maronite Order (O.L.M), with its 300-year tradition and principles, and wishing to contribute to the development of the medical sector and health services in Lebanon, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) created the School of Medicine and Medical Sciences, with the express purpose of providing initial and a continuing education of general practitioners and specialists.
Devoted to helping the development of competent professionals and, simultaneously, to be at the service of all, the School participates in the advancement of knowledge in the field of health and aims to be nationally and internationally recognized for to the excellent quality of its teaching programs.

# School of Music and Performing Arts
(Affiliated to the Faculty of Arts and Sciences)
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/academics)
### On October 31, 1970, from among all the universities in the Middle East and North Africa, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik was the first to undertake the initiative of founding, within the Faculty of Letters, the Institute of Musicology.
It would be unnecessary to highlight how much Lebanon and the whole region was in need of such initiative. This Institute was established, thanks to the efforts deployed particularly by Rev. Fr. Louis Hage, Founder and Director of the Institute from 1970 until 1986, and Rev. Fr. Etienne Sacre, President of the University between 1968 and 1974.    
  
[ Read More](https://www.usek.edu.lb/school-of-music-and-performing-arts/overview)
